items.title: Heart, the Heretic: The Forgotten Visionary Jane Ellen Harrison on Critical Thinking, Emotional Imagination, and How to Fix the World
items.description: "If we are to be true and worthy heretics, we need not only new heads, but new hearts, and, most of all, that new emotional imagination... begotten of enlarged sympathies and a more sensitive habit of feeling."

items.title: Legendary Cellist Pablo Casals, at Age 93, on Creative Vitality and How Working with Love Prolongs Your Life
items.description: "The man who works and is never bored is never old. Work and interest in worthwhile things are the best remedy for age."

items.title: The Art of Conversation: Timeless Do’s and Don’ts from 1866
items.description: "In disputes upon moral or scientific points, ever let your aim be to come at truth, not to conquer your opponent. So you never shall be at a loss in losing the argument, and gaining a new discovery."

items.title: How to Love the World More: Artist and Poet Rachel Hébert’s Breathtaking Catalogue of Gratitudes
items.description: Here we are, living these lives bright and perishable as a poppy, hard and shimmering as obsidian. We know that they are entirely improbable, that we bless that bright improbability with each flash of gratitude for it all, that if we pay attention closely and generously enough we are always repaid in gladness, that it is the handle of the door to the world. items.title: The Only Three Distinctions Between People
items.description: It may be that consciousness evolved to sieve the relevant from the incomprehensible allness of all there is, to parse the world into concepts and find an organizing principle for the chaos of them. Our cognitive inheritance is a restless yearning to fathom how things cohere and where they belong, a yearning we have given shape to in laws and labels, weights and balances, hierarchies and categories. It has served us well, this instinct to categorize in order to contain, giving us music, the laws

items.title: How to Touch the Nothingness Behind Everything: Kahlil Gibran on the Seven Selves
items.description: A self is a forest. A self is a ship. A self is an illusion, and yet it is the place where we live, the costume the naked soul wears to survive in the world. Above all, a self is a sum of selves, contextual as a chameleon, conflicted as a parliament. Which self takes the reins of our character and conduct at any given time is a function of which animating passion takes possession of us. items.title: The Third Thing: Poet Donald Hall on the Secret to Lasting Love
items.description: "Third things are essential to marriages, objects or practices or habits or arts or institutions or games or human beings that provide a site of joint rapture or contentment."

items.title: How to Bear Your Desolations
items.description: "You may have to break your heart, but it isn’t nothing to know even one moment alive."

items.title: How to Criticize with Kindness: Philosopher Daniel Dennett on the Four Steps to Arguing Intelligently
items.description: "Just how charitable are you supposed to be when criticizing the views of an opponent?"

items.title: Silence and Love
items.description: Music is the hand of silence cupped to hold the feeling of being alive, lifted to the lips and tasted. What differentiates music from noise is the touch of silence — the deliberate interstices between the tones, the still points in the rush of sound. items.title: Vladimir Nabokov on What Makes a Good Reader
items.description: "A good reader, a major reader, an active and creative reader is a rereader."

items.title: The Relief of Rock Bottom: George Orwell and the Secret Springboard of Success
items.description: It happens to everyone — to kings and paupers, to astronauts and poets. Nothing will protect you from it — not money, not love, not perfect health — for it spares no life that is fully lived, not the sunniest or the most privileged or the best planned. It begins with the wall — the one you hit over and over and over, not breaking through. And then, after the exhausted collapse, the bottom. items.title: The Paradox of “Finding Yourself”
items.description: "The self is a style of being, continually expanding in a vital process of definition, affirmation, revision, and growth..."

items.title: The Most Powerful Attitude You Can Take Toward Your Life and the Life of the World
items.description: "This fluke, single, huge, cross-indexed, thermodynamic experiment of a story that the world has been inventing to tell itself at bedtime is still in embryo. It's not even the outline of a synopsis of notes toward a rough draft yet."

items.title: Where the Joy Is
